titleText.es: ¿Sabíais que te pueden echar físicamente del SIGGRAPH?
titleText.en: Did you all know that they can physically throw you out of SIGGRAPH?
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish title text switches from plural informal sabíais to singular informal te. The official English source leaves the number of listeners unspecified and also includes ‘actually,’ which the Spanish version omits.

regions.labelEs: ESA GRÁFICA EXPLICABA EL EFECTO HALL CUÁNTICO. AHORA, SI ME DISCULPAN UN MOMENTO, ESTA GRÁFICA MUESTRA LA PLUVIOSIDAD SOBRE LA CUENCA DEL AMAZONAS...

excludedUnits.rationale: Hall is the physicist's English surname inside the technical name efecto Hall cuántico, not Spanish lexical vocabulary. The surrounding Spanish words retain their own contextual word cards.

applications.explanationEn: Explicaba uses the -aba background-past form because the chart's explanatory role is presented as part of the setup rather than as a separately bounded event.
Si opens the courteous request, me identifies the speaker, disculpan addresses several listeners, and un momento states the brief time requested.

regions.labelEs: SI NO PARAS DE DECIR "SI ME DISCULPAN UN MOMENTO", LA GENTE TARDARÁ UN RATO EN DARSE CUENTA DE QUE LES ESTÁS MOSTRANDO DIAPOSITIVAS ALEATORIAS.

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces a genuinely possible condition, and paras uses the ordinary present form for one familiar listener; no negates that action between them.
Paras changes parar for one familiar listener, de supplies the required link, and decir stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
This quoted occurrence uses disculpan because the courteous formula is addressed to several listeners; the other four words complete the same fixed request.
Tardará keeps the whole dictionary form tardar and adds -á for a future action by one person, group, or thing.
Tardará gives the future form, un rato supplies the duration, en is the required link, and darse is the unchanged action form with se attached.
Se attaches directly to the unchanged verb dar, making the single printed word darse.
Darse begins the fixed expression darse cuenta here, so its contextual meaning comes from that complete expression rather than literal self-giving.
Darse cuenta forms the fixed expression for realizing, and de que introduces the full statement that follows as what is realized.
Les treats the members of la gente collectively as the several people receiving what is shown.
Les identifies the plural receivers and sits before estás, the first verb changed for the listener; the following ongoing-action form stays outside this placement pattern.
Estás changes estar for one familiar listener, and mostrando is the -ando action form that presents the showing as in progress.

cards.noteEn: Here gráfica is a visual display of data, not the feminine form of an adjective meaning ‘graphic.’
Explicaba is a past form of explicar. Its -aba ending presents the explaining as part of the background or an ongoing past situation, without marking a separate completed endpoint.

example.en: The guide was explaining the map.

cards.answerEn: Use the preterite for a completed event and the imperfect for background, an ongoing situation, or something that used to happen.
cards.noteEn: Think of a story: the preterite answers “What happened next?” The imperfect answers “What was happening?”, “What were things like?”, or “What used to happen?” These two names describe how the speaker presents an event, not simply how long it lasted.
cards.questionEn: Spanish has two common ways to talk about the past. When do you use each one?

example.en: While I was walking, it started to rain.

cards.answerEn: quantum; relating to quantum physics (masculine singular)
cards.noteEn: Cuántico describes phenomena governed by quantum physics, especially at atomic and subatomic scales. Its ending changes to cuántica with a feminine singular noun.

cards.questionEn: How can you politely ask one formal listener or several listeners to excuse a brief interruption?
cards.answerEn: Say si me disculpa un momento to one formal listener, or si me disculpan un momento when addressing several people as ustedes.
cards.noteEn: Si means ‘if,’ me identifies the speaker asking to be excused, and un momento gives the brief time requested. Disculpa addresses one formal listener. Disculpan addresses any group in Latin America and a formal group in Spain; an informal group in Spain would use disculpáis. The parentheses in the prompt show that the final n is added only for the disculpan form.

example.es: Si me disculpa un momento, voy a buscar el informe.
example.en: If you'll excuse me for a moment, I am going to get the report.

cards.answerEn: you excuse; you pardon (addressing a group)
cards.noteEn: Disculpan is a present form of disculpar used with ustedes, the usual plural ‘you’ throughout Latin America and a formal plural ‘you’ in Spain. In si me disculpan, it makes a polite request for the listeners' brief patience.

example.en: Will you excuse me for a moment?

cards.noteEn: Pluviosidad is a technical or formal word for how much rain a place receives over a period.
Sobre can introduce the geographical area across which something is measured or happens. This is different from sobre meaning ‘about’ a topic.

example.es: La tormenta avanza sobre la costa.
example.en: The storm moves over the coast.

cards.noteEn: A cuenca is the land area whose water drains into the same river or body of water.

example.es: El río recoge agua de toda la cuenca.
example.en: The river collects water from the whole basin.

cards.noteEn: Spanish writes de followed by the masculine singular word el as the single word del.

example.es: El color del coche es rojo.
example.en: The color of the car is red.

cards.noteEn: Spanish commonly uses el Amazonas for the Amazon River. Cuenca del Amazonas therefore names the broad area drained by that river.

example.es: El Amazonas cruza una región enorme.
example.en: The Amazon crosses an enormous region.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cards.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cards.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.
Paras is the present form of parar used for tú, one familiar listener. Before de and another action verb, it means that the listener stops doing that action.

cards.promptEs: parar de + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone stops doing an action?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of parar, then de, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The plus signs in the prompt show the order of the three pieces. The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Only parar changes for the person and time: paro de hablar, paras de hablar, pararon de hablar. De is required even though English does not translate it separately.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links parar to the action that stops
cards.noteEn: Spanish requires de between a form of parar and the following action verb. English does not translate this linking word separately.
Tardará keeps the complete verb tardar and adds -á to place the time-taking in the future for one person, group, or thing.

example.en: The repair will take an hour.

cards.questionEn: How do you say what someone will do in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Keep the action verb in its dictionary form and add a future ending such as -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, or -án.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. The ending identifies the person: sentir plus -á gives sentirá, and ver plus -á gives verá. A few common verbs change their stem, but use the same endings.

cards.questionEn: How do you say how long someone takes to do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of tardar, the amount of time, en, and the action verb in its dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Tardar changes for who takes the time. En links the time to the action and normally has no separate English word in this pattern.

example.en: I take ten minutes to arrive.

cards.answerEn: while; a short or unspecified period of time
cards.noteEn: Un rato refers to an imprecise stretch of time. Its length depends on the situation rather than on a fixed number of minutes.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links the time taken to the action
to realize; to notice (as part of darse cuenta)
cards.noteEn: Darse combines the dictionary form dar with se attached. It does not mean ‘to give oneself’ here: darse cuenta is the complete fixed expression for realizing or noticing something.

example.es: Marta puede darse cuenta del error.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.

cards.promptEs: darse cuenta de (que) + hecho o situación
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone realizes or becomes aware of something?
cards.answerEn: Use the matching small pronoun, a form of dar, cuenta, and then de before what is realized.
cards.noteEn: The small pronoun and dar must match the person: me doy cuenta, te das cuenta, se da cuenta, nos damos cuenta, and so on. Use de before a noun and de que before a full statement. Cuenta is not translated separately in this expression.

example.es: Nos dimos cuenta de que faltaba una llave.
example.en: We realized that a key was missing.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes darse cuenta, “to realize”
cards.noteEn: Cuenta can mean an account, bill, or calculation. In darse cuenta, it is part of a fixed expression and is not translated separately.

example.es: Ella se dio cuenta muy tarde.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word here; introduces what is realized after darse cuenta
cards.noteEn: After darse cuenta, de introduces the fact or thing that becomes clear. Before a full statement, Spanish normally uses de que.

example.es: Se dio cuenta de que era tarde.
example.en: She realized that it was late.

cards.noteEn: Que introduces a clause after verbs such as creer, saber, esperar, or decir. English often uses “that,” but may leave it unstated.

example.en: I think that Ana is coming.

cards.answerEn: to them; marks them as the people receiving something
cards.noteEn: Les identifies more than one receiver. It normally appears before a verb that changes for the person and time, although it can attach to some unchanged verb forms and positive commands.

cards.promptEs: me/te/le/nos/os/les delante del verbo que cambia
cards.questionEn: Where do you put the short word that identifies who receives something?
cards.answerEn: Put me, te, le, nos, os, or les before the first verb that changes for the person and time.
cards.noteEn: The slashes in the prompt mean to choose the one receiver word that fits. A verb that changes for the person and time is often called a conjugated verb: estoy rather than the dictionary form estar. In a multiword verb phrase, the receiver word goes before that changed verb, so les estoy enviando places les before estoy, not between estoy and enviando.

example.en: I am sending them a photo.

cards.answerEn: Use a form of estar followed by an action word ending in -ando or -iendo.
cards.noteEn: Estar changes to show who is doing the action: estoy, estás, está, and so on. For most verbs, replace -ar with -ando (hablar → hablando) and replace -er or -ir with -iendo (comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo). This is similar to English “am/is/are doing.”
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone is in the middle of doing something?

cards.noteEn: Mostrando is the ongoing-action form of mostrar. Regular verbs ending in -ar replace -ar with -ando to make this form.
Diapositiva can name one image or page shown as part of a presentation. The plural diapositivas refers to several such slides.
Aleatorias describes several feminine things selected or arranged without a planned pattern. The -as ending matches a feminine plural noun such as diapositivas.
